title: Autellix: An Efficient Serving Engine for LLM Agents as General Programs
technique: Program-level scheduling (PLAS for single-threaded, ATLAS for multi-threaded, non-clairvoyant) with preemption on cumulative program service time plus data-locality-aware load balancing

optimized_metrics.evidence: an LLM serving system that treats programs as first-class citizens to minimize their end-to-end latencies.
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: Average latency for different LLM serving systems across four real-world workloads

optimized_metrics.evidence: Autellix focuses on three primary objectives: (1) improving overall program's end-to-end latency, for users, (2) maximizing GPU utilization for providers, and (3) mitigating program starvation to improve fairness, measured via 95th and 99th percentile latencies.
mitigating program starvation to improve fairness, measured via 95th and 99th percentile latencies.

headline_claim.text: Autellix improves throughput of programs by 4-15× at the same latency compared to state-of-the-art systems, such as vLLM.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 12 (program-level token latency vs request rate)
Fig 5-6 waiting vs execution time ratio
max programs/s at fixed latency, Fig 12

metric_definitions.definition_quote: a single-threaded program's end-to-end latency comprises three components: (1) waiting time, the total queuing time of a program's LLM calls on the engine; (2) execution time, the cumulative feedforward time of LLM calls; and (3) interceptions, time spent waiting for external interrupts such as tool calls or human input.
metric_definitions.notes: Program E2E = waiting + execution + interceptions; interceptions (tools/humans) excluded from what Autellix can optimize.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Existing LLM serving systems focus on request-level metrics, such as Time-to-First-Token (TFTT) and Time-per-Output-Token (TPOT), also referred to as token latency. However, these metrics overlook end-to-end latency for agentic programs. To that end, we introduce program-level token latency, defined as the total program response time divided by the number of tokens generated
metric_definitions.notes: Normalized program completion time (s/token); for multi-threaded programs: 'critical path response time divided by the total tokens across all threads' (footnote 2). Called simply 'latency' in evaluation. 'Throughput' = highest program arrival rate (programs/s) sustainable at a given program-level token latency.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: waiting time, the total queuing time of a program's LLM calls on the engine
metric_definitions.notes: Cumulative per-program queueing, used for the Fig 2 HoL analysis.

slo_spec: No explicit SLO thresholds; compares latency-vs-request-rate curves and reads throughput at equal latency.
load_regime: request-rate sweep (programs/s) over ShareGPT, BFCL, LATS, Mixed; single-engine and multi-engine
tradeoff_acknowledged: Preemptive scheduling can reduce average latency but risk starving long programs (tail); MLFQ had poor P95/99 on ShareGPT; Autellix lower tails in 7 of 8 scenarios.
hardware: A100-SXM4-80GB GPUs with NVLink; 1, 4 and 8 GPUs per engine
workloads: ShareGPT chatbot, BFCL function calling (ReAct), LATS MCTS, Mixed; multi-threaded DAG programs
extractor_notes: Explicit request-level vs program-level distinction: paper says TTFT/TPOT overlook program E2E and defines per-token normalised program latency. 'Throughput' headline is load at equal program-level token latency, not tokens/s. Tail (P95/P99) is reported and fairness is measured by tails.
